description: Sixteen gate outputs, one per learned note: each output goes high while the note learned into its cell is held on the incoming polyphonic pitch and gate pair

params.text: Turns that cell's output into a toggle, switching on and off on each fresh press of its note in place of following the held note; learning or clearing that cell turns this back off

inputs.text: The polyphonic pitch cable the cells are matched against, and the cable that notes are learned from; it usually comes from a MIDI-CV module or from a Zones output
The polyphonic gate cable; a channel counts as held at 1V or more, and a rising edge here is what an armed cell captures as its note

outputs.text: 10V while the note learned into that cell is held on any channel of the input, or while that cell is toggled on in latch mode, and 0V otherwise, including for a cell with no note

notes: a cell is learned by clicking it and playing the note on the incoming cable, or by clicking it and typing a letter from A to G, a # for a sharp and a digit for the octave, then Enter
control-click, or command-click on a Mac, arms a cell for sequential learning, so each note captured arms the next cell and a whole row of pads can be mapped in one pass
Escape, or clicking the armed cell again, cancels a learn and leaves that cell as it was; Backspace or Delete clears the cell to two dashes and its output then stays at 0V
the same note is never mapped twice: learning a note into one cell clears it from whichever other cell held it
a module fresh from the browser comes up with a chromatic run, C2 in the first cell up to D sharp 3 in the sixteenth, meant as something to learn over
a cell shows a short line above its note name while that note is held on the input, and a line below while its own output is high; with latch on for that cell, the two can differ
the first output is the top cell of the display's left column and the sixteenth is the bottom of its right column, running down each column in turn
the sixteen cells are drawn inside one display widget rather than as separate controls, so no help line can be reached by clicking a cell
only the first sixteen channels of the input cables are read
menu: Add an expander — places a PadX immediately to the right of this module, or to the right of the last expander already chained there
Clear unpatched cells — clears the note from every cell whose own gate output has no cable in it, leaving the patched cells alone
Invert latches — turns latch on for every cell that had it off, and off for every cell that had it on
Factory presets — on Rack's own Preset submenu: ready-made cell mappings, chromatic and white-key or black-key runs, the stock pad maps for two controllers, and Unmapped for a clean slate
